title: Derivative of Gaussian noise
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose that both are square-integrable for standard Gaussian product measure and that the positive-time Gaussian noise difference quotients of $f$ converge to $g$ in $L^2$ as time tends to zero. For any $\rho\in(-1,1)$ with $\rho\ne0$ and any $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the Gaussian noise average of $f$ as a function of its correlation parameter is differentiable at $\rho$, with derivative equal to the Gaussian noise average of $g$ at $\rho$, divided by $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ and $g$ are square-integrable for standard Gaussian product measure
$g$ is the $L^2$ limit of the positive-time Gaussian noise difference quotients of $f$
